On the surface, this 24-episode series, directed by MohammadReza Moeini, is a fictional narrative about the death of a village elder, a dispute among the locals, a historical legacy, and a web of family and social relationships—but on a deeper level, it strives to bring to the television screen a region that has rarely had the chance to be seen in the full richness of its cultural, historical, and human potential.
🔸"Asbad" can be seen as an attempt to shift the angle of vision—moving away from an image that views a region solely through the lens of its problems, and drawing closer to people who, like all Iranians, have their own lives, loves, families, conflicts, aspirations, work, migration, hopes, and concerns. This shift in perspective is no small feat for television. Margaret Hamilton, an American scientist and one of the pioneers of software engineering who played a key role in landing the first American astronauts on the Moon, has died at the age of 90. She led a team of experts who designed and developed the software used in NASA's Apollo space missions. MIT, confirming Hamilton's death, announced that she passed away on Wednesday, the eighth of Mehr 1405, corresponding to September 30, 2026. In a statement, the institute described Hamilton as one of the pioneers of computer science who played an important role in developing the field before software engineering became a widespread profession. Hamilton worked at MIT from 1959 until the mid-1970s and headed the software engineering division. The group she managed designed the guidance and control software for the Apollo 11 spacecraft, which played a decisive role in the historic landing of Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the Moon in 1969. During this mission, the spacecraft's computer encountered a processing overload moments before landing, but the software designed by Hamilton's group was able to continue the landing operation by prioritizing tasks. Barack Obama, the former president of the United States, awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2016 in recognition of Hamilton's scientific achievements and her role in advancing space technology. @VahidOOnLine📡 @VahidOnline

Reuters reported on Thursday, 16 Mehr, that the number of ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz has fallen to its lowest level in more than two months, following a surge in attacks on oil tankers last week. Citing data and analysis from the analytics firm Kpler, Reuters reported that only 7 commercial vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday — the lowest figure since the first of Mordad. Crude oil transit through the strait also dropped 27 percent from the wartime peak the previous week, falling to at least 10.1 million barrels per day, equivalent to 74 percent of the pre-war level. According to Kpler analysts, most of this decline is attributable to ship-to-ship transfers of cargoes in the Sea of Oman. According to Reuters, however, exports from the coasts of the Sea of Oman and the Red Sea rose to 6.7 million barrels per day — more than double the pre-war level — helping to offset the reduced supply through the Strait of Hormuz. Kpler data shows the number of transiting ships rose to 10 on Wednesday, but remained far below the more than 20 vessels seen on Sunday and Monday. The report comes after attacks on oil tankers passing through the Strait of Hormuz last week reached their highest weekly level since the start of the Iran war. Before the war began on the ninth of Esfand last year, roughly 125 large commercial ships — including oil tankers, gas carriers, bulk carriers, and container ships — passed through the Strait of Hormuz daily. entry.title:
[FarsNA] A mouth that opened at the wrong time
🔹In a clear pond, two ducks and a…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @FarsNA

A mouth that opened at the wrong time

🔹In a clear pond, two ducks and a turtle were neighbors, and a deep friendship and bond had formed between them. Time passed, and due to drought, the water in the pond began to dry up.

🔹The ducks, seeing that it was no longer possible to stay, came to the turtle to say goodbye and migrate to another body of water.

🔹The turtle lamented with sorrow and tears and said: "Waterlessness is far more dangerous for me, a slow-moving animal, than for you, and my life is impossible without any water. It is not the way of chivalry that you abandon me in this waterlessness; think of me and take me along with you."

🔹The ducks said: "Being apart from you is hard for us too, but you have a flaw: you take the advice of friends lightly and you don't shut your mouth at the right time!

🔹If you want us to take you too, there is one condition: we will bring a stick, we two will hold its two ends in our beaks, and you hold the middle of the stick firmly with your mouth so we can take flight. In the sky, no matter what people say and whatever shouts they raise, do not open your mouth!"

🔹The turtle promised and said: "I will obey and will not open my lips until the destination."

🔹The ducks brought the stick, the turtle gripped its middle firmly with its teeth, and they leapt into the air. As they were passing over a village, people's eyes fell on this amazing scene. An uproar rose among the people and they shouted: "Look! How the ducks are carrying the turtle through the air with a stick!"

🔹Hearing the clamor, the turtle could not endure it and became angry. Thinking it would say something to them, it opened its mouth and said: "May your eyes be blinded!"

🔹But as soon as it opened its lips, the stick was released from its mouth, and it fell from the height of the sky to the ground.

#حکایت@Farsna

- The "Mizan" news agency, affiliated with the judiciary of the Islamic Republic, reported that Alireza Sepahi Badjani, known as Alireza Sepahi, was executed at dawn on Monday, 13 Mehr 1405, in Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan.
- Alireza Sepahi's lawyer had warned the previous day of the imminent danger of his execution, announcing that Sepahi's family had been summoned to meet with him and that he had been transferred to solitary confinement.
- Before his execution, Alireza Sepahi married his fiancée by telephone. Mahshad Kashani, a 22-year-old student living in Isfahan, was also arrested during the Dey 1404 protests and sentenced to five years of discretionary imprisonment; she is being held in the women's prison in Dolatabad, Isfahan.
- Alireza Sepahi had been scheduled to be executed at dawn on Tuesday, 6 Mordad 1405, alongside Abolfazl Sepahi Badjani — his cousin — and Amirhossein Safari Hosseinabadi, in Malek Shahr, Isfahan, in a public execution, but he suffered a heart attack from stress before the sentence could be carried out, and his execution was postponed.
- Alireza Sepahi is the fourth citizen arrested during the Dey 1404 protests to be executed over the past week, following the issuance of a statement by 46 countries condemning executions in Iran. Siavash Jamshidi Kheirabadi was executed on Saturday, 11 Mehr, in Shahrekord, and Ali Hemmati Sistani and Majid Nikandish were executed on Wednesday, 8 Mehr, in Mashhad.
- The case known as the "Midan Alikhani" case is connected to the protests on the evening of 18 Dey 1404, which took place in the area of Midan Alikhani, between Malek Shahr and Kaveh in Isfahan. The security institutions of the Islamic Republic claimed that four Basij and special unit forces were killed during these protests.
- With the execution of Alireza Sepahi, six defendants in the "Midan Alikhani" case have now been executed. Erfan Esfandiari and Golmohammad Mohammadi were executed on 28 Tir in prison. Abolfazl Sepahi and Amirhossein Safari were hanged in public on 6 Mordad in "Midan Alikhani," and Ghaem Hosseini was executed on 29 Mordad in the Central Prison of Isfahan (Dastgerd).

Coinciding with the start of the World Week Against the Death Penalty, the judiciary of the Islamic Republic executed Alireza Sepahi and Alireza Raeisi, two of those arrested during the nationwide protests of Dey 1404, in the case known as "Alikhani Square." These two protesters were executed today, Monday 13 Mehr 1405, in Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan. Shahrzad Shahbazi, a lawyer and the defense attorney for Alireza Sepahi, wrote in this regard: "Alireza Sepahi's retrial was granted by the Supreme Court, but the parallel branch (Branch Two) of the Isfahan Revolutionary Court, without holding a hearing, rejected the retrial in less than 48 hours." Alireza Sepahi had previously been scheduled to be executed in the early hours of Tuesday, 6 Mordad 1405, along with Abolfazl Sepahi Badjani and Amirhossein Safari Hosseinabadi, but before being transferred to the execution site, he suffered a stroke and was taken to the hospital due to the severity of his physical condition. Two days later, after receiving medical treatment, he was returned to Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan. Published evidence regarding cases related to the Dey 1404 protesters shows that the death sentences issued so far have been accompanied by serious legal and juridical ambiguities, and in the vast majority of cases, the fundamental principles of a fair trial — including the right to effective access to a lawyer, public proceedings, independent examination of evidence, and full observance of the guarantees stipulated in the Code of Criminal Procedure — have not been observed. Therefore, the issuance and execution of death sentences against protesters, rather than being a sign of an independent and impartial judicial process, indicates that the death penalty has been turned into a tool for creating fear and terror in society and preventing the recurrence of protests. dadban4@mamlekate

entry.title:
[FarsNA] The consequence of befriending deceivers
🔹A crow, a wolf, and a jackal…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @FarsNA

The consequence of befriending deceivers

🔹A crow, a wolf, and a jackal lived in a thicket alongside a lion, and they got by on the leftovers of his kills.

🔹One day, a camel that had fallen behind from a caravan came to that thicket to graze. When the camel came upon the lion, it bowed, and the lion granted it safety, saying it could live in peace under his protection.

🔹Some time later, the lion was badly wounded in a fight with an elephant, collapsed in his cave, and lost the strength to hunt. The animals around him were left helpless with hunger. The crow, looking for a way out, proposed to his companions that they find a way to get the lion to eat the camel.

🔹The jackal said, "The lion has granted him safety, and breaking one's word is shameful." The crow replied, "Leave it to me; I'll devise a scheme so the camel himself walks into being sacrificed."

🔹The crow went to the lion and, with smooth talk, won him over and promised to arrange things so that there would be no need to break the covenant.

🔹Then he went to the wolf, the jackal, and the camel and said, "The Sultan's life is in danger; come, let us show our loyalty and offer ourselves. The lion does not eat our flesh, but the custom of service is fulfilled."

🔹They all went to the lion. First the crow stepped forward and offered himself, but the wolf and the jackal cried out, "You're scrawny and your flesh tastes foul!" Then the jackal volunteered, and the others called his flesh stinking. It was the wolf's turn, and they deemed his flesh harmful.

🔹The simple-hearted camel, seeing this staging, thought to himself that if he too made an offer, the companions would, following the same custom as before, come up with some excuse and the lion's protection would hold. So he came forward and said, "My body is a sacrifice for the Sultan; my flesh is pure and will fill everyone." No sooner had he finished speaking than all three animals said with one voice, "He speaks the truth!" and immediately fell upon him and made him their prey.

#حکایت@Farsna

#Virtual_Space_Roaming🔰Let's read the table so we don't become a mere shopfront🔺Maybe the development model is something other than buying Ronaldo!🔸Iran's young caravan — a nation that has been through war — in days when even coming and going through the skies was difficult for it, reached sixth place in Asia with 19 golds, 18 silvers, and 15 bronzes;◽It became the best country in West Asia by a wide margin◾It reeled in 6 more gold medals than the previous edition of the competitions◽Its girls claimed a 15-medal share of the caravan's 52 medals◾And it was only 3 more golds away from achieving the best result in its history...Hats off to them and may they stay in good health.🔸Saudi Arabia, too, reached twentieth place in the table with 3 golds, 2 silvers, and 9 bronzes — above Singapore and below Vietnam; it maintained the gap it has always had with Iran, and likely, with the rise of Iranian female athletes in recent years, that gap will only widen.🔸Of course, I have always avoided/avoid this kind of induction, but since for several years the most inefficient and backward development model — one that views every manifestation of development as a mere shopfront — has been used to humiliate Iranians, I say: Perhaps the "development model" should be something other than buying foreign players at ten times their market price for a seductive show in the domestic league... It is where the Portuguese Ronaldo cannot take the field in place of a Saudi athlete and win a medal that the true measure of nations' progress finally becomes clear... Just as in wartime, the true measure of a cheap military force — one whose software, hardware, and infantry arise from its own soil, science, and national awareness — is revealed against the world's greatest military power; and the impurity of an expensive army becomes apparent when, after being branded a "milking cow" and buying up countless fighter jets and Patriot systems and hiring hundreds of thousands of mercenaries from other countries, they are ultimately deployed to fight against a besieged land with the least possible military logistics — and get stuck in the mud.🔸Which problem does sports solve? She described the charges brought in this case as "extremely serious."
